result.stdout:
Usage:
  srtx inspect  [--rules rules.json]
  srtx optimize [mode] [--rules rules.json] [--output rules.optimized.json]
  srtx generate [--rules rules.json] [--sieve rules.sieve] [optimization]
  srtx preview  [--rules rules.json] [--script-name name] [--reconciled-rules reconciled-rules.json] [--candidate-rules candidate-rules.json]
  srtx deploy   [--plan deployment-plan.json] [--history-limit count] [--no-prune-history]
  srtx rollback [--plan deployment-plan.json] [--force]
  srtx history list
  srtx history show <script-name> [--sieve restored.sieve]
  srtx history restore <script-name|latest|original> [--dry-run] [--force]
  srtx history delete <script-name|original> [--dry-run]
  srtx history prune [--dry-run]

Optimization: conservative, balanced, aggressive; aliases -o, -oo, -ooo.
Synchronization options: --script-name, --adopt-compatible, --preserve-compatible, --dry-run.
ManageSieve options: --sieve-host, --sieve-port, --sieve-username, --sieve-password, --sieve-security-mode override TRANSIEVER_SIEVE_*.
Generated managed rules include provider UI metadata comments for Open-Xchange-compatible rule editors.
Preview preserves the current active script name by default; deploy activates the previewed candidate after creating any required server-side backup.
Deploy prunes inactive SieveRuler history automatically, keeping the oldest backup plus the newest retained history scripts.
History restore creates a fresh backup before restoring a retained SieveRuler version, latest backup, or original state.
History delete and prune remove inactive history in SieveRuler's reserved history namespace; matching names are managed regardless of who created them. Prune keeps the active script and scripts outside that namespace.
Review artifacts: --reconciled-rules, --candidate-rules, --candidate, --server-snapshot, --plan.

  srtx inspect  [--rules rules.json]
  srtx optimize [mode] [--rules rules.json] [--output rules.optimized.json]
  srtx generate [--rules rules.json] [--sieve rules.sieve] [optimization]
  srtx preview  [--rules rules.json] [--script-name name] [--reconciled-rules reconciled-rules.json] [--candidate-rules candidate-rules.json]
  srtx deploy   [--plan deployment-plan.json] [--history-limit count] [--no-prune-history]
  srtx rollback [--plan deployment-plan.json] [--force]
  srtx history list
  srtx history show <script-name> [--sieve restored.sieve]
  srtx history restore <script-name|latest|original> [--dry-run] [--force]
  srtx history delete <script-name|original> [--dry-run]
  srtx history prune [--dry-run]

Optimization: conservative, balanced, aggressive; aliases -o, -oo, -ooo.
Synchronization options: --script-name, --adopt-compatible, --preserve-compatible, --dry-run.
ManageSieve options: --sieve-host, --sieve-port, --sieve-username, --sieve-password, --sieve-security-mode override TRANSIEVER_SIEVE_*.
Generated managed rules include provider UI metadata comments for Open-Xchange-compatible rule editors.
Preview preserves the current active script name by default; deploy activates the previewed candidate after creating any required server-side backup.
Deploy prunes inactive SieveRuler history automatically, keeping the oldest backup plus the newest retained history scripts.
History restore creates a fresh backup before restoring a retained SieveRuler version, latest backup, or original state.
History delete and prune remove inactive history in SieveRuler's reserved history namespace; matching names are managed regardless of who created them. Prune keeps the active script and scripts outside that namespace.
Review artifacts: --reconciled-rules, --candidate-rules, --candidate, --server-snapshot, --plan.
